_about: The Omega42 Glossary and the protocol terms (lexicon.html). The General Glossary gives established meanings: those of the Core's Words Explained, and further terms written by the Navigator from standard usage. Protocol terms give Omega42's own vocabulary with its authority; where the Core defines a term, the Core governs and this list points to it. The Omega42 Lexicon of readings of existing concepts is records/lexicon/lexicon.json (Companion Part 211). Definition types: established, adopted, adapted, proposed, speculative.

types.adopted: an existing definition used by Omega42 unchanged
types.adapted: an existing concept deliberately given an Omega42 meaning
types.proposed: a new term introduced by Omega42
types.speculative: a provisional meaning used to explore a possibility

general.meaning: The capacity of an agent to act and to bring about effects.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: A likeness between two things in some respects, used to understand one through the other; it does not show they share a structure.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: a statement taken as the starting point of a system, from which its theorems are proved.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: The relation in which one event or condition brings about or contributes to another.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: the view that a statement is true when it fits without contradiction into a whole system of statements, rather than by matching something beyond the system.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: A statement believed or proposed to be true but not yet proved.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: Subjective experience: there being something it is like to be a system. Its nature and basis are an open question across philosophy and science.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: A statistical association between two quantities; on its own it does not show that one causes the other.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: The single digit obtained by adding the digits of a positive whole number repeatedly; it equals the number modulo 9, with 9 in place of 0.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: the view, associated with Baruch Spinoza, that mind and matter are two aspects of one underlying reality rather than two separate substances.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: Properties of a whole that arise from the interactions of its parts and are not found in the parts alone.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: The capacity of a system to do work; its SI unit is the joule (J = kg m² s⁻²).
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: In thermodynamics, a measure of the number of microscopic arrangements compatible with a state; in information theory, the average uncertainty of a source in bits. The two are related but not interchangeable.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: The study of knowledge: what it is, how it is justified, and where its limits lie.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: Karl Popper's criterion: a statement is scientific when some possible observation could show it false.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …: each term is the sum of the two before it.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: The dimensionless strength of the electromagnetic interaction, about 1/137.036, measured, not derived from theory.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: A state that a transformation leaves where it is.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: the question of whether, and how, our choices are our own when the world follows laws.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: A set with an operation that is associative, has an identity element and gives every element an inverse.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: Fluent output from an AI system that is false or unsupported, such as a citation to a source that does not exist.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: David Chalmers's name for the question of why and how physical processes give rise to subjective experience.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: a method for finding things out, valued for what it helps you discover rather than as a proof.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: A proposed explanation or statement put forward for testing.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: Kurt Gödel's proof that any consistent formal system rich enough to describe arithmetic contains true statements it cannot prove from within.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: A measure of the reduction of uncertainty, counted in bits: one bit settles a choice between two equally likely possibilities.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: open to, and checkable by, anyone, so that it does not depend on a single person's view.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: A quantity or property that does not change under a specified transformation.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: A one-to-one correspondence between two structures that preserves their operations: two structures that are the same up to renaming.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: David Hume's observation that no set of facts about how things are can, by itself, establish how things ought to be or what they are worth.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: An AI system trained on large amounts of text to predict and generate language; the kind of system that serves as a Navigator.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: in Einstein's relativity, the directions light can travel from a point; in Omega42 every place lies on one.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: Max Tegmark's proposal that physical reality is not described by a mathematical structure but is one.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: Arithmetic in which numbers wrap around after reaching a fixed modulus: modulo 9, 7 + 5 = 12 leaves 3.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: The default assumption of no effect or no difference, against which a test is made.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: the part of philosophy that asks what exists and what it is to be. Omega42's premise is an ontology: one structure, and nothing else.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: The set of states visited from a starting state by repeatedly applying a transformation.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: The probability, if the null hypothesis were true, of a result at least as extreme as the one observed.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: The property of repeating exactly after a fixed number of steps, the period.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: A rearrangement of a set in which each element goes to exactly one place and none is lost.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: the view, associated with Friedrich Nietzsche, that every view of the world is a view from somewhere, so that there is no view from nowhere.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: The study of the structures of experience as experienced, associated with Edmund Husserl.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: The period of the Fibonacci sequence taken modulo a number; for 9 it is 24.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: Plato's view that the things we see are shadows or copies of a deeper realm of perfect, unchanging forms.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: the philosophy, associated with William James and Charles Sanders Peirce, that judges ideas by what they let us do and understand.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: the starting supposition from which everything else is drawn. Omega42's premise is that its one structure is all that exists.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: A unit whose powers run through every unit; modulo 9 the primitive roots are 2 and 5.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: the view, from Heraclitus to Alfred North Whitehead, that reality is made of happenings rather than of fixed things.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: The record of where something came from and how it reached its present form.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: the ancient teaching, from Pythagoras and his followers, that number is the substance of all things.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: A rule that defines each term of a sequence from earlier terms, such as the Fibonacci rule F(n + 1) = F(n) + F(n − 1); also the return of a state or pattern.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: Repeating a study or computation independently to see whether the result holds.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: The property of a result that others can obtain again from the same data and method.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: The remainder left when an integer is divided by the modulus; modulo 9 the residues are 0 to 8.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: a system that counts something as true because the system itself produced it. Omega42 is closed, with nothing beyond it, but it is not self-confirming.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: The International System of Units, maintained by the BIPM and defined since 2019 by seven exact constants.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: the idea that our world is a computer simulation run by something beyond it.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: The view that what science captures is the structure of the world, its relations, rather than the intrinsic nature of things.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: Invariance under a specified transformation: something that stays the same when a stated change is made.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: A system whose laws are symmetric settling into a state that is not.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: A statement proved from axioms and earlier theorems by valid steps.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: reasoning inside an imagined situation to see what follows from it, without needing the situation to be real.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: everything there is, taken as one whole, with nothing left over and nothing beyond.
general.source: Core, Introduction, Words Explained

general.meaning: The material an AI system learned from; it shapes what the system writes and how.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

general.meaning: A residue that has a multiplicative inverse; modulo 9 the units are 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8.
general.source: Standard usage, written by the Navigator

protocol.definition: The moment the Striker offers a question for navigation, in answer to the Introduction's invitation, by asking for a navigation, or by striking a domain directly.
protocol.authority: Core, Part 0 and the Strike Law (Rule 4)

protocol.definition: The person who brings the question and keeps the judgment of what a reading means and is worth.
The AI system that runs the protocol: computes the coordinate, writes the reading and declares its status, and never judges for the Striker.

The space Omega42 keeps for your judgment, where you decide what a reading means and what it is worth; no reading can enter it. The Aperture Theorem is the protocol's proof that this space cannot be closed.
In Omega42, agreement between readings, questions or AI systems that is greater than chance would produce, counted and reported apart from coherence.
The position twelve steps from an anchor on the 24-cycle: Antipode = P((anchor + 12) mod 24). Modulo 9 it is the negative of the state, so a digit and its Antipode add to 9 or to 0.
The position on the 24-cycle that a question's counts give it; the four arms are read from it.
The six positions P3, P7, P11, P15, P19, P23 of the 24-cycle, whose values 3, 9, 6, 6, 9, 3 lie in the 3-layer.
protocol.authority: Core (the Crown and its sum, CDT-A)

protocol.definition: The units modulo 9, {1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8}: the residues that have an inverse. With the Crown set {3, 6, 9} it partitions the nine residues.
P0, and the seed pair {2, 5} from which the recurrence unfolds the 24-cycle.
The tiers of a statement: CDT-A mathematical fact; CDT-B constructed interpretation inside Omega42; CDT-C speculative proposition. A fourth kind, external correspondence, is kept apart.
That the canonical 24-cycle and its 81-state family are all that exists: stipulated for the thought experiment, explored for its consequences, not graded.
The proposed underlying layer of recurrent mathematical structure from which Omega42 investigates states, transformations and relationships.
protocol.authority: Proposed by ChatGPT 6 (OpenAI), 20 November 2026; not yet in the Core or the Companion

protocol.definition: The proposed layer of existence shaped by historical dependence, choices, inherited conditions, relationships and the consequences of actions.
The proposal that existence begins with one distinction from a balance; modulo 9 the central antipodal pair (4, 5) is (−1/2, +1/2), one unit apart.
